# Mirror contacts across systems: HubSpot & Twilio

**Pattern:** Two-System Sync · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers process-orchestration work end to end across HubSpot, Twilio, Google Sheets and Google Drive.

It moves through 17 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. Weekly Schedule
2. Load Previous Snapshot
3. Fetch Changes (Google Drive)
4. Normalize Records
5. Upsert into Google Sheets
6. Advance Watermark
7. Persist Watermark (HubSpot)
8. Save Execution Metadata
9. Tag Pipeline Metadata
10. Align Field Names
11. Stamp Processing Time
12. Sort Jobs Newest First
13. Guard Non-Empty type
14. Cap Batch Volume
15. Summarize Run Stats
16. Append Audit Row (HubSpot)
17. Send Summary to Twilio

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Twilio — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing process-orchestration work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Weekly Schedule → Load Previous Snapshot → Fetch Changes (Google Drive) → Normalize Records → Upsert into Google Sheets → Advance Watermark → Persist Watermark (HubSpot) → Save Execution Metadata → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Align Field Names → Stamp Processing Time → Sort Jobs Newest First → Guard Non-Empty type → Cap Batch Volume → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (HubSpot) → Send Summary to Twilio → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Twilio

## Use it for

- Teams keeping HubSpot and Twilio aligned by hand for process orchestration
- Process orchestration work where "Fetch Changes (Google Drive)" is still a manual step before HubSpot
- Process orchestration work that only reaches HubSpot on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps HubSpot and Twilio in step for process orchestration, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed HubSpot or Twilio call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 19 nodes in this process-orchestration build
- Every process-orchestration run leaves an audit row behind, alongside HubSpot
- Fans the same result out to Google Sheets in the same run, for process orchestration
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 19 nodes for process orchestration before wiring HubSpot

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2; Google OAuth2 / service account; HubSpot private-app token; Twilio SID + token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

The pipeline is incremental, not full-refresh: it stores a watermark (the last-seen timestamp) and only asks the source for records newer than that, which is what keeps a scheduled re-run cheap instead of re-pulling the entire dataset every time. The tradeoff is that a failed watermark write must be safe to retry — which is exactly why the destination write is an upsert, not a plain insert.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Manually roll the watermark back and re-run — confirm the upsert makes the replay safe (no duplicates).
2. Trigger a reconcile mismatch on purpose and confirm the drift alarm fires.
3. Point the source at a different platform and see how little else in the workflow has to change.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**HubSpot private-app token**
HubSpot → Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → create app → copy the token.
_Gotcha:_ Grant the CRM scopes you need; legacy API keys are deprecated and will not work.

**Google OAuth2**
Google Cloud Console → enable Drive API → OAuth2 client or Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Service Accounts have their own empty Drive — share the target folder with it.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Twilio SID + token**
Twilio Console → Account Info → Account SID + Auth Token.
_Gotcha:_ The `from` number must be one you own in Twilio. Trial accounts only send to verified numbers.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your process orchestration process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- HubSpot: a private-app token carrying only the CRM scopes these nodes use — legacy API keys are deprecated and over-broad.
- Twilio: an API key/secret pair scoped to messaging, not the account SID and auth token.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Google Drive: scope the credential to the one folder this workflow writes to, not `drive.readonly` across the account.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole process-orchestration payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
